p1s.what: Re-derived from raw counts the comparator-arm spread is 12/42 - 1/16 = 28.5714% - 6.2500% = 22.3214 pts, which prints 22.3, not 22.4. heterogeneity() computes spreads from ALREADY-ROUNDED per-cohort percents (reads r['percent'], which wilson() rounds to 1 dp); Python's round-half-to-even sends 6.25 -> 6.2, so 28.6 - 6.2 = 22.4. This is the only one of eight heterogeneity spreads in the document where rounding before subtracting changes the printed digit (death 7.1/5.7, LR TAF15 3.6, metastasis 8.9/18.5, TKI 53.9, prevalence 13.4 all agree with the raw derivation). The defect is systematic in the generator even though it currently bites once. Fix: compute the spread from unrounded proportions and round once at the end.
